Hi Samuel / Maya —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we kick off the evaluation work: 

Summary of needs
- 2 primary flows: clinical intake form parsing (structured JSON output) and intent-to-action routing (tool/function calls).
- High bar on JSON schema compliance (strict keys, types) and deterministic field-level accuracy for a small set (~30 canonical fields).
- Concern: downstream regression risk when we push quantized/low-latency variants.

Redwood recommendation (initial run)
- Baseline: redwood-serve-14b-8k-qat for quality vs cost balance.
- Speed variant: redwood-serve-3b-q4 for low-latency fallbacks in the router.
- For the critical routing use-case, we will test redwood-toolcaller-7b (function-call optimized) to validate tool invocation reliability.

Deliverables we will provide this week
1) Eval kit: prompt set (50+ examples), target JSON schema (schema_examples.json), and grading rubric.
2) Small benchmark run on your sample (we asked for 500 records) and a quality/regression checklist.
3) Mutual action plan (MAP) with dates for tech deep dive, sample handoff, and initial eval report.

Action items (who/what)
- Samuel / Maya: confirm we can share the 500-record de-identified sample by Friday and any PII redaction constraints.
- Priya: share MAP & HubSpot record (done) and set up the tech deep dive with Aditya.
- Aditya: prepare function-calling tests and schema-enforcement harness.
- Neha: coordinate CS touchpoints for staging and SLO / rollback policy conversations.

Attachments: helix_sample_manifest.csv (manifest), schema_examples.json, redwood_eval_checklist.xlsx.

Proposed deep dive slots: Tue 3/20 10:00–11:00 PT or Wed 3/21 15:00–16:00 PT. Please confirm one.

Thanks — will follow up with the eval kit link and HubSpot reference.

Subject: RE: Helix Health - structured-output eval kickoff & model recommendations

Samuel / Maya — quick technical note ahead of Tue's deep dive. Below is a concise plan for the eval harness and things we'll measure.

Model variants to test (initial battery)
- redwood-serve-14b-8k-qat: baseline for quality and schema fidelity.
- redwood-serve-3b-q4: latency-optimized fallback; will test for regression on critical fields.
- redwood-toolcaller-7b: function-call optimized variant for routing reliability.

Schema enforcement approach
- We run a two-stage validator: 1) strict JSON Schema (types/required keys), 2) semantic checks (e.g., normalized date formats, code lookups).
- Examples: missing required `patient_id` => hard fail; `dosage` free-text with ambiguous units => soft fail and flag for human review.
- We'll produce per-field precision/recall and an overall schema-pass rate.

Function-calling & retry strategy
- Basic flow: model returns {tool_name, args}. Redwood runtime attempts the tool call up to 3 times with exponential backoff (100ms, 300ms, 900ms) before marking it failed.
- We'll track: call_success_rate, retry_count_histogram, end_to_end_latency_p95, and error classifications (timeout, malformed_args, downstream_error).
- For your 99.5% requirement we will run an extended reliability test (1000 simulated calls) to validate the combined model+runtime SLO.

Evaluation artifacts we'll hand back
- Per-model CSV with example gold vs. predicted JSON, per-field metrics, and a short issues register with representative failures.

Notes on performance tuning
- Quantized paths (q4/q8) may change tokenization timing and occasionally alter numeric formatting in outputs; part of the harness includes a micro-regression detector that highlights fields with >2% delta in pass rate between baseline and speed variant.

If you have any specific tool endpoints (internal APIs) you want us to call during the test, send endpoint docs and auth details (we will run calls in a dedicated staging VPC).

Looking forward to the deep dive.

— Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
